items.stem: What does the Trustee Positions page maintain?

options.text: The 7 elected trustees, each with their position and boundary map
Every staff member's job assignment and proxy address
The list of vendors and their representatives
The AAD security groups that grant editing rights

items.explanation: Trustee Positions maintains the 7 elected trustees with their position and boundary maps.

misconceptions.b: Staff and job assignments are people-and-roles data, not trustee positions.
misconceptions.c: Vendor Reps are a separate entity from elected trustees.
misconceptions.d: Data Owners are the access constructs; trustee positions are org-structure governance data.

items.stem: On the Wards page, what is maintained for each ward?

options.text: The set of wards and each ward's relationship to its elected trustee
The municipal-division hierarchy and parish assignments
The attendance-area map for each school
The standalone-group membership for each resident

items.explanation: The Wards page maintains the set of wards and the relationship of each ward to the elected trustee who represents it.

misconceptions.b: Municipal Divisions are a separate org-structure entity; wards carry the trustee relationship.
misconceptions.c: Attendance areas link to schools, not to wards-and-trustees.
misconceptions.d: Standalone Groups are hand-maintained access lists, unrelated to wards.

items.stem: The trustee-and-ward data maintained in SDM is primarily used by which consumer?

options.text: The external district site, which shows residents their elected representatives
The HRAD system of record
The SMTP / email-notification configuration
The Selenium UI test harness

items.explanation: Both Trustee Positions and Wards describe data used for the external (public-facing) district site.

misconceptions.b: HRAD is the system of record for schools/staff, not the consumer of trustee data.
misconceptions.c: Email configuration is unrelated to publishing trustee-and-ward data.
misconceptions.d: The test harness is not a data consumer.

items.stem: The district redraws its electoral boundaries, moving a ward into a different trustee's area. Which actions keep SDM correct?

options.text: Update the affected trustee positions' boundary maps, then re-point the moved ward to its new trustee on the Wards page
Delete the ward and recreate the trustee in HRAD
Only edit the Wards page; trustee positions never change
Edit the ward's attendance-area map on the Schools page

items.explanation: Trustee Positions and Wards are siblings: a boundary change on a position usually means re-pointing the affected ward's trustee relationship so the two stay in step.

misconceptions.b: Trustees are elected seats maintained in SDM, not records created in HRAD.
misconceptions.c: Boundary maps live on the trustee positions; ignoring them leaves the governance map stale.
misconceptions.d: Attendance areas link schools, not wards to trustees.

items.stem: Why are Trustee Positions and Wards classified as org-structure data rather than people-and-roles (Staff) data?

options.text: They describe elected seats and the geography they cover, not HR staffing
They store each trustee's payroll and benefits
They are managed by the Help Desk for temporary access
They are AAD security groups that grant editing rights

items.explanation: There are exactly 7 elected trustee seats, each tied to a boundary and its wards — this is org-structure/governance data, distinct from the Staff/HR people-and-roles area.

misconceptions.b: SDM does not hold payroll/benefits; trustees are elected seats, not HR records.
misconceptions.c: Temporary access via Entra groups is the Standalone Group / Help Desk flow, unrelated here.
misconceptions.d: Security groups are Data Owners; trustee positions are governance org structure.

items.stem: In one or two sentences, explain how Trustee Positions and Wards relate to each other and why keeping them in sync matters.
rubric: States Trustee Positions maintains the 7 elected trustees with position/boundary maps
States Wards maintains wards and each ward's relationship to its elected trustee
Notes the data feeds the external district site, so an out-of-sync ward-to-trustee link is publicly visible / points residents at the wrong representative
items.sampleAnswer: Trustee Positions holds the 7 elected trustees with their boundary maps, and Wards ties each ward to the trustee who represents it; because this data drives the external district site, a stale boundary or wrong ward link would publicly point residents at the wrong representative.
